title: 2026-11-14 — A `gate.py control` controls file: a `run` holding a newline takes a `'''` literal

data.head: ## 2026-11-14 — A `gate.py control` controls file: a `run` holding a newline takes a `'''` literal

body: A controls file is TOML: a `run` command that spans lines must be written as a multi-line literal `'''…'''`. A single-quoted `'…'` literal holding a newline is not TOML, and the tool refuses the whole file before anything runs (measured at 2026-11-14-bundled-fonts: the first `control-1.toml` refused, re-written with `'''` and re-fired).

The session added two stand checks and changed no production code, manifest, workflow, committed check or dependency.
A cross-OS readings check holds each of the six served tasks (Counter, Flight Booker, Timer, CRUD, Cells, the load page) in both layout modes, at boot and after one acting step by click, type or advance, and compares the driver's answer digests of snapshot (every part of a paged screen), lint and actions against one 48-row table.
That table read the same on linux x86_64, windows x86_64 and macOS aarch64 in CI; before, only the two committed Counter checks were read on the three OSes.
A families check reads that sans-serif, serif, monospace, system-ui, an unavailable named family, cursive and fantasy all lay out in the stand's one bundled font, DejaVu Sans, with the same text extent, in both layout modes; nothing is deferred.
Measured: the bundled font is registered for four generic families only; the others reach it by fallback, since it is the only font loaded, so the claim that it is registered for every generic family is false while the reading holds.
The fonts-unavailable answer is kept unchanged, and the stand checks' three-round repeat takes both new checks by their stand_ prefix with no count moved.

The session added two test-only stand checks to blitz-tests and changed no production file, manifest, dependency, workflow, CI step or committed check file.
The first reads the driver's answer digests for the six served tasks (counter, flight-booker, timer, crud, cells, load) in both layout modes, at boot and after one step by click, type or advance, over snapshot (every part), lint and actions, against a committed 48-row table of digests; CI read the same table on linux x86_64, windows x86_64 and macOS aarch64.
Before it only the two committed Counter checks were read cross-OS; the new check holds no shot and prints nothing.
The second reads the text extent of seven font families (sans-serif, serif, monospace, system-ui, an unavailable named family, cursive, fantasy) on the stand's one bundled font, DejaVu Sans, with system fonts off: all read the sans-serif extent, by fallback to the only loaded font, not by registration.
The fonts-unavailable refusal is kept unchanged; nothing was deferred or retired.

body_fields.fact: The six served tasks (counter, flight-booker, timer, crud, cells, load) are read on every CI OS (linux x86_64, windows x86_64, macOS aarch64) by one stand check. It compares the driver's answer digests for snapshot (every part), lint and actions, at boot and after one acting step in both layout modes, to one committed table, with no shot and no kept check file.

In both layout modes, every generic font family (sans-serif, serif, monospace, system-ui, cursive, fantasy) and an unavailable named family read the bundled font's sans-serif text extent in a stand check. The reason is fallback to the font context's only font, not a registration per family.

On a font context that holds one font, a control that removes one generic family's registration is vacuous, because the fallback reaches that font anyway. The red control for a font-family reading is a font context that holds other fonts.
